summary: Berkeley hills steel lookout built on Grizzly Peak in 1924 and razed in 1960; sources give three heights and two reasons. A 1962 survey description reports a steel tower on the summit in good condition, so the removal date is unclear. No source describes the site today.

facts.design: 7x7 observation cabin on an open steel X-brace tower, with a Mission-style watchman's house beside it
facts.status_note: Register and 1960 Tribune items give a 1960 removal; a 1962 survey description reports a steel tower on the summit in good condition, so the removal date is unclear. No source describes what, if anything, remains at the summit today.
facts.agency: Contra Costa Hill Fire Protective Association, with the City of Berkeley

events.note: A major blaze in September 1923 swept into the Berkeley hills and led to the tower's construction
Steel tower raised on the summit
Glen Gadbury named fire warden, with a warden's house on the peak
Harry Piper was the watchman in 1925
State aid withdrawn; city manager proposed Berkeley pay the full lookout salary (March 16, 1933 item)
Gene Smith, the tower's third boss, left with the moving day set at June 30
Razing approved to take effect June 30 when the city's lease expires; the register says removed in 1960
Coast and Geodetic Survey station description says the steel tower was recovered in good condition on the summit; conflicts with the 1960 removal date

notes_for_editor: Heights disagree: 35 ft (1924 item), 40 ft (1925 item and register), 60 ft (April 13, 1960 Tribune item), and 40 ft again (April 20, 1960 Tribune item). The record's height_m 10.7 matches the 35-foot figure; it is left unchanged and not written to facts. The register calls the funder the Contra Costa Hill Fire Protective Association; 1924 papers call it the Contra Costa Hills Fire Protection Committee. 1924 papers name Gadbury as warden; the 1960 report calls Piper the first man on the hill. The register gives funding withdrawal as the 1960 reason; the 1960 paper gives maintenance no longer needed, given by the acting city manager. Removal date conflict: the register gives 1960 removal and the April 1960 Tribune reports approve razing effective June 30, but a 1962 Coast and Geodetic Survey station description on the Forest Lookouts page calls the steel tower recovered in good condition on the summit; the story states the conflict and does not pick a date. The Claremont post says the signs were newly installed and that Oakland stepped up patrols; it does not say who installed them, so the story does not say. One WebSearch found no removal record and no description of the site today; the Claremont Canyon 'lookouts' are roadside spots and no source ties them to the tower, so no access fact is written. Possible follow-up: Berkeley Public Library local history, the Berkeley Historical Society, and a check of the 1962 survey record, not checked. No new photos found.
